```{r}
library(tidyverse)
visitors <- read_csv("data/UK-visitor-numbers.csv")
#Q1(a)
visitors |> count(region)
#Q1(b)
visitors |> count(admission, setting)
#Q2
visitors |> summarise_all(class)
#Q3
visitors |> arrange(desc(n_2021)) |> head(n=10)
#Q4(d)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 == 565772)
#Q4(e)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 > 1000000) |> count() - 22
#Q5(f)
visitors |> filter(n_2022 > 50000 & n_2022 < 100000) |> count() - 50
#Q5(g)
visitors |> count(region) |> filter(n > 50)
#6
mean(visitors$n_2022, na.rm = TRUE)
median(visitors$n_2022, na.rm = TRUE)
#Q7
#outside <- visitors |> filter(setting == "O") |> select(n_2022)
#outside
#mean(outside$n_2022, na.rm = TRUE)

evaluate_mean <- function(dataframe, setting_letter){
  temp_df <- dataframe |> filter(setting == setting_letter) |> select(n_2022)
  mean(temp_df$n_2022, na.rm = TRUE)
}

outside_mean <- evaluate_mean(visitors, "O")
inside_mean <- evaluate_mean(visitors, "I")
mixed_mean <- evaluate_mean(visitors, "M")

max_mean <- max(outside_mean, inside_mean, mixed_mean)

if (outside_mean == max_mean) {
  print("Outside attractions has largest amount of mean visitors in 2022.")
} else if (inside_mean == max_mean){
  print("Inside attractions has largest amount of mean visitors in 2022.")
}else{
  print("Mixed attractions has largest amount of mean visitors in 2022.")
}

#Q8
visitors_2021 <- visitors |> select(n_2021)
max(visitors_2021, na.rm = TRUE)
min(visitors_2021, na.rm = TRUE)

#9
IQR(visitors_2021$n_2021, na.rm = TRUE) #needed $n_2021 to get numerical values for IQR to function

#after reading hints for this question, realised this is not sufficient, as needed IQR for each of the four nations in the UK

#6(h)
visitors |>
  summarise(
    mean_2021 = mean(n_2021),
    med_2021 = median(n_2021)
  )
#yields NA as result

#6(i) NA - not available, previous questions yields this value as no mathematical operation can be executed when there are null values

#6(j)
visitors |>
  summarise(
    mean_2021 = mean(n_2021, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_2021 = median(n_2021, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
#na.rm removes all the NA values in the column

#7(k)
visitors %>% 
  group_by(setting) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_2022 = mean(n_2022),
    med_2022 = median(n_2022)
  )
#mean significantly greater has it accounts for extreme values, whereas median does not

#8(l)
visitors |>
  summarise(
    max_2021 = max(n_2021, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_2021 = min(n_2021, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#9(m)

#below is the code from the hints in terms of finding IQRs
visitors_with_nations <- visitors %>%
  mutate(
    nation = case_when(
      region == "Northern Ireland" ~ "Northern Ireland",
      region == "Scotland" ~ "Scotland",
      region == "Wales" ~ "Wales",
      TRUE ~ "England"
    )
  )

visitors_with_nations %>% 
  group_by(nation) %>%
  summarise(
    IQR_2022 = IQR(n_2022)
  )

#tourist attractions from each nation
visitors_with_nations |>
  group_by(nation) |> 
  count()
```

##Warmup Question Answers
1. "count(visitors)" - 348 attractions
2. attraction - chr, n_2021 - dbl, n_2022 - dbl, admission - chr, setting - chr, region - chr
3. "arrange(visitors, desc(n_2022))" - The Crown Estate, Windsor Great Park
4. "filter(visitors, attraction == "National Museum of Scotland")" - Free
5. "filter(visitors, setting == "O", region == "Yorkshire and the Humber", admission == "Members", n_2022 > "100,000")" - Fountains Abbey Estate, Kirkstall Abbey, RHS Garden Harlow Carr
